title: Data on Inmates Enrolled in Employment Preparation Scheme, Granted Leave and Secured Employment upon Release
what_it_is: Data on Inmates Enrolled in Employment Preparation Scheme, Granted Leave and Secured Employment upon Release

sections.label: Work release scheme inmates
sections.summary: Inmates on the scheme serve the tail-end of their sentence in a work release centre, with some allowed home leave and most released inmates securing employment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Inmates emplaced on the scheme are required to serve the tail-end of their sentence in a work release centre administered by Singapore Prison Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Those who are doing well and have support from their family, may be allowed to go on weekend home leave or long home leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: As at 31 January 2024, 71 of the 339 inmates had gone or are currently allowed to go on weekend home leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Another 35 had gone through or are currently on long home leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: And 204 of the 339 inmates have been released.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Among them, 196 had secured employment at the point of release.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: In fact, what we have seen, has been encouraging, where not only the inmates are having the opportunity, but the employers are coming, quite strongly, to support this scheme.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: And we are also very happy that the social service agencies (SSAs) are also coming on board, working together with our specialists, to make sure that not only do we provide that employment, training opportunity, but looking at a throughcare rehabilitation and re-integration process.
